arxiv-2009-10527.title: Wilker and Huygens type inequalities for mixed trigonometric-hyperbolic functions
arxiv-2009-10527.creator: Yogesh J. Bagul 1 , Ramkrishna M. Dhaigude 2 , Barkat A. Bhayo \coraut 3 , Vinay M. Raut 4
arxiv-2009-10527.description: A 2020 arXiv research paper by Yogesh J. Bagul 1 , Ramkrishna M. Dhaigude 2 , Barkat A. Bhayo \coraut 3 , Vinay M. Raut 4. Motivated by the work of Sándor [ 19 ] , in this paper we establish a new Wilker type and Huygens type inequalities involving the trigonometric and hyperbolic functions. Moreover, in terms of hyperbolic functions, the upper and lower bounds of sin ⁡ ( x ) / x \sin(x)/x and tan ⁡ ( x ) / x \tan(x)/x are given.

Leto, F. Verrecchia, N. Ricard, S. Di Pippo, R. Middei, A. V. Penacchioni, R. Ruffini, N. Sahakyan, D. Israyelyan, S. Turriziani
arxiv-2108-07255.description: Abstract Blazars research is one of the hot topics of contemporary extragalactic astrophysics. That is because these sources are the most abundant type of extragalactic γ \gamma -ray sources and are suspected to play a central role in multi-messenger astrophysics.

arxiv-2206-13637.title: Utility Theory for Sequential Decision Making
arxiv-2206-13637.creator: Mehran Shakerinava, Siamak Ravanbakhsh
arxiv-2206-13637.description: Abstract The von Neumann-Morgenstern (VNM) utility theorem shows that under certain axioms of rationality, decision-making is reduced to maximizing the expectation of some utility function. We extend these axioms to increasingly structured sequential decision making settings and identify the structure of the corresponding utility functions.

arxiv-2301-01773.title: LARGE-EDDY SIMULATIONS OF TURBULENT COMPRESSIBLE SUPERSONIC JET FLOWS USING DISCONTINUOUS GALERKIN METHODS
arxiv-2301-01773.creator: Diego F. Abreu 1,†,∗, Carlos Junqueira-Junior 2, Eron T. V. Dauricio 1,‡ and João Luiz F. Azevedo 3
arxiv-2301-01773.description: Abstract In this work, a discontinuous Galerkin scheme is employed to perform LES simulations of supersonic jet flows. A total of four simulations are performed with different meshes and order of accuracy. The number of degrees of freedom from the simulations varies from 50 × 10 6 50\times 10^{6} to 400 × 10 6 400\times 10^{6} .

arxiv-2306-14949.title: Optical Identification of the Shortest-Period Spider Pulsar System M71E hst1pass, MAAT
arxiv-2306-14949.creator: Zhuokai Liu, Subo Dong
arxiv-2306-14949.description: Abstract M71E is a spider pulsar (i.e., a millisecond pulsar with a tight binary companion) with the shortest known orbital period of P = 53.3 P=53.3 min discovered by Pan et al. (2023). Their favored evolutionary model suggests that it bridges between two types of spider pulsars, namely, it descended from a “redback” and will become a “black widow”.

arxiv-2311-10413.title: Quantum Enhancement in Dark Matter Detection with Quantum Computation
arxiv-2311-10413.creator: Shion Chen, Hajime Fukuda, Toshiaki Inada, Takeo Moroi, Tatsumi Nitta, Thanaporn Sichanugrist
arxiv-2311-10413.description: Abstract We propose a novel method to significantly enhance the signal rate in qubit-based dark matter detection experiments with the help of quantum interference. Various quantum sensors possess ideal properties for detecting wave-like dark matter, and qubits, commonly employed in quantum computers, are excellent candidates for dark matter detectors.

arxiv-2408-01869.title: MALADE: Orchestration of LLM-powered Agents with Retrieval Augmented Generation for Pharmacovigilance
arxiv-2408-01869.creator: Jihye Choi, Somesh Jha, Anivarya Kumar, David Page
arxiv-2408-01869.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Jihye Choi, Somesh Jha, Anivarya Kumar, David Page. In the era of Large Language Models (LLMs), given their remarkable text understanding and generation abilities, there is an unprecedented opportunity to develop new, LLM-based methods for trustworthy medical knowledge synthesis, extraction and summarization. This paper focuses on the problem of Pharmacovigilance (PhV), where the significance and challenges lie in identifying Adverse Drug Events (ADEs) from diverse text sources, such as medical literature, clinical notes, and drug labels.

arxiv-2504-16244.title: Accounting for spillover when using the augmented synthetic control method: estimating the effect of localized COVID-19 lockdowns in Chile Volume: XX
arxiv-2504-16244.creator: Taylor Krajewski ∗ Department of Biostatistics, University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill, Chapel Hill, North Carolina, U.S.A, Michael Hudgens ∗ Department of Biostatistics, University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill, Chapel Hill, North Carolina, U.S.A
arxiv-2504-16244.description: Abstract The implementation of public health policies, particularly in a single or small set of units (e.g., regions), can create complex dynamics with effects extending beyond the directly treated areas. This paper examines the direct effect of COVID-19 lockdowns in Chile on the comunas where they were enacted and the spillover effect from neighboring comunas.

pmc-10587987.title: Sintilimab plus anlotinib as second‐ or third‐line therapy in metastatic non‐small cell lung cancer with uncommon epidermal growth factor receptor mutations: A prospective, single‐arm, phase II trial
pmc-10587987.creator: Kaiyan Chen, Yanjun Xu, Zhiyu Huang, Xiaoqing Yu, Wei Hong, Hui Li, Xiaoling Xu, Hongyang Lu, Fajun Xie, Jun Chen, Youzu Xu, Yun Fan
pmc-10587987.description: BackgroundPatients with non‐small‐cell lung cancer (NSCLC) and uncommon EGFR alterations typically have worse treatment outcomes than patients with classically EGFR‐mutated NSCLC. This study aimed to investigate the efficacy and safety of PD‐1 blockade with sintilimab plus anti‐angiogenic treatment with anlotinib in patients with NSCLC harboring uncommon EGFR mutations.

pmc-13005840.creator: Rodrigo Suarez-Silva, Manuel Saucedo-Bazalar, Manuel Ramirez Saenz, Renato D. La Torre Ramirez, Esteban Caycho, Gisella Orjeda
pmc-13005840.description: A progressive decline in populations of Neltuma pallida (Humb. & Bonpl. ex Willd.) C.E. Hughes & G.P. Lewis (algarrobo) has been documented in Peru. pmc-13365340.creator: Lingyun Wu, Weifeng Jiang
pmc-13365340.description: BackgroundRetinopathy, as a manifestation of systemic microvascular dysfunction, has been increasingly recognized as a potential indicator of cerebrovascular disease. However, evidence regarding the association between retinopathy and stroke risk remains inconsistent. This meta-analysis aimed to quantitatively evaluate the relationship between retinopathy and the risk of stroke.
